region.text: the Oudalan province without the one cell Mali's own (modern-frontier) Cliopatria shape already held before the war: the 42 cells mali-federation/ledger/6 moved to Mali as 'the western portion of the Agacher Strip'; the page gives no area and the modern frontier keeps Oudalan in Burkina Faso

events.note: 22 December 1986: the ICJ divided the Agacher Strip: 'Mali received the more-densely populated western portion and Burkina Faso the eastern section centered on the Beli', a strip the page puts at about 160 km long, with no area or coordinates. Ledger 6 gives Mali the whole Oudalan province (42 cells, about 10,900 km2), far more than the western part of one border strip, and Mali's Cliopatria shape (the modern frontier) holds none of it. The province goes back to Burkina Faso; the western strip Mali won is too small and unplaced on the page to draw. [Reviewer: region cut by Mali's 1985 Cliopatria shape, so the one Oudalan cell Mali held before the war (and kept, as the ICJ gave Mali the western part) stays Malian instead of passing to Burkina Faso.]

1 January 1986: Aruba 'seceded' from the Netherlands Antilles; 'In 1986, Aruba became a constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands'. There is no Aruba dossier, so the cell is drawn as Dutch land until one exists (the Antilles' keyframe now ends in 1985, keyframe_overrides/1, and its ledger 16 leaves the cell with nobody).

The page dates the exits: St. Lucia 1979 'Independence', British Honduras 1981 'Independence', Brunei 1984 'Independence'. The 1969 shape now ends in 1969, as its own note says 'valid for 1969 only' (reviewer: was 1978; the page dates Fiji 'Independence' 1970, Bahamas 1973, Grenada 1974, Dominica and Solomon Islands 1978, so the 1970-1978 keyframes re-added them too; the drawn map of 1970-1979 is unchanged, conflict bookkeeping drops by about 300 cell-years).
